source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting structural defects in a bridge maintenance report

1. Start with the maintenance records.
2.
completion:
Collect and review all existing maintenance records of the bridge, including past inspection reports, defect logs, previous repair work, service life assessments, and intended maintenance plans. Ensure that these records are complete, accurate, and up-to-date before proceeding to analyse them.

3. Conduct a thorough visual inspection.
Perform a systematic visual examination of the bridge structure. Check for cracks, spalling (chipping or flaking of concrete), exposed reinforcement, rust staining, delamination, efflorescence (white crystalized deposits), settlement, misalignment, joint failures, corrosion of metal components, and any other visible signs of deterioration.

4. Use non-destructive testing (NDT) methods.
Utilize NDT methods such as ultrasound testing, ground-penetrating radar, magnetic particle inspection, and half-cell potential mapping to detect hidden defects, measure the depth and extent of cracks, assess the integrity of concrete, and determine the level of corrosion in steel components.
